hypotheses.basis: Rule R7 uses 'only when' which can be read as establishing a necessary condition (a constraint) without establishing a sufficient one. 'Permits only when X' means: if not-X, then not-permitted (violation). But it does NOT mean: if X, then permitted. Permission when X holds might require additional unstated conditions or come from other rules. R7 is thus a prohibition rule, not a permission-granting rule.

hypotheses.basis: Rule R7 can be read as granting a permission scoped to the ownership condition, without implying that the absence of the condition constitutes a violation under R7. 'Permits only when X' establishes the scope of the permission (it applies only in case X) but does not itself create a prohibition for non-X cases. Non-X cases are simply outside R7's scope and governed by other rules or defaults.
